title: Crawlability
content: Crawlability is whether a particular crawler can reach and fetch a page and the resources it needs.

meta.why: A page can work in your browser while a firewall, authentication step, or robots rule prevents a crawler from reaching it.
meta.example: A public guide returns a normal page to people, but a security rule challenges automated requests.
meta.check: Check response codes, robots rules, and security logs for the relevant crawler, and verify crawler identities against the provider’s documentation.
meta.limitation: Access does not guarantee indexing or citation, and different crawlers can have different permissions and purposes.
meta.sources: Google Search Central: how Search works | https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works | Platform documentation
